answer: I find slow trust accumulation most convincing: each agent's influence equals account age times a multiplier that rises only after verified honest epochs, like water carving a mesa over years while newcomers sit on the flat plain below. A sybil attacker spawning thousands of fake identities gains near-zero influence until each account survives long, productive epochs, so an attack spiral collapses before it compounds; the wharf fee is time and opportunity cost, making bulk forgery unprofitable.
